subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(b) of the supplied proof of the parent theorem intcpt_flat_limit_integer_multiplicity ("apply (H) to f(z,S) := g(z)"), with the details filled in. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact, Grassmannian.instCompactSpace); H^n := μHE[n]; unitBallVolume n is the extended-real volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal; μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^n⌞T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)); p_S := Grassmannian.project S = Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S; t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ (operator norm of p_S − p_P). (H) denotes the hypothesis ∫ f dW_k → θ₀ ∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G.
1. Let F(z,S) := g(z) on ℝ^N × G. F = g ∘ Prod.fst is continuous.
2. support F = (support g) × G ⊆ tsupport g × G, and tsupport g × G is closed (product of closed sets), so tsupport F ⊆ tsupport g × G (closure_minimal).
3. tsupport g is compact by hypothesis and G is compact, so tsupport g × G is compact (IsCompact.prod); F has compact support (closed subset of a compact set). Hence F defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) with f(z,S) = g(z).
4. tsupport f ⊆ tsupport g × G ⊆ B°_5(0) × G, so (H) gives ∫ f dW_k → θ₀ ∫ f dv(P).
5. μ_{W_k} = (W_k).measure.map Prod.fst. Prod.fst is measurable and g is continuous (hence a.e.-strongly measurable), so by integral_map ∫ g dμ_{W_k} = ∫ g(z.1) dW_k(z) = ∫ f dW_k for every k.
6. v(P) = (H^n⌞P.plane).map (y ↦ (y,P)); the map y ↦ (y,P) is measurable and f is continuous, so by integral_map ∫ f dv(P) = ∫_{P.plane} f(y,P) dH^n(y) = ∫_{P.plane} g dH^n.
7. Substituting 5 and 6 into 4 gives ∫ g dμ_{W_k} → θ₀ ∫_{P.plane} g dH^n.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(c) of the supplied proof of the parent theorem intcpt_flat_limit_integer_multiplicity (T.plane is isometric to ℝ^n, on which μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure). Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact, Grassmannian.instCompactSpace); H^n := μHE[n]; unitBallVolume n is the extended-real volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal; μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^n⌞T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)); p_S := Grassmannian.project S = Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S; t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ (operator norm of p_S − p_P).
1. dim T.plane = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane). Choose an orthonormal basis B of the subspace T.plane indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis reindexed along finCongr of this equality) and let L := (T.plane).subtypeₗᵢ ∘ B.repr.symm : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ^N. L is a linear isometry, L(x) ∈ T.plane for every x, and L(B.repr v) = v for every v ∈ T.plane.
2. Put ι(x) := a + L(x). Then dist(ι x, ι y) = ‖L x − L y‖ = ‖L(x − y)‖ = ‖x − y‖, so ι is an isometry.
3. For every s: ι(B_s(0)) = T.plane ∩ B_s(a) and ι(B°_s(0)) = T.plane ∩ B°_s(a). Indeed, a + L x ∈ T.plane because a ∈ T.plane, and dist(a + L x, a) = ‖L x‖ = ‖x‖; conversely, if y ∈ T.plane and dist(y,a) ≤ s (resp. < s), then y − a ∈ T.plane, x := B.repr(y − a) has ‖x‖ = ‖y − a‖ ≤ s (resp. < s), and ι x = a + (y − a) = y.
4. By Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, H^n(ι(S)) = μHE[n](S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n, and μHE[n] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
5. volume(B_r(0)) = ofReal(r^n)·volume(B°_1(0)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, r ≥ 0, finrank = n) and volume(B°_r(0)) = ofReal(r^n)·volume(B°_1(0)) (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, r > 0; this form needs no nontriviality, so n = 0 is included). volume(B°_1(0)) = unitBallVolume n by definition and ofReal(r^n) = (ofReal r)^n.
6. Combining 3–5: H^n(T.plane ∩ B_r(a)) = H^n(ι(B_r(0))) = volume(B_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n·(ofReal r)^n, and likewise for the open ball.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the notation paragraph of the supplied proof of the parent theorem intcpt_flat_limit_integer_multiplicity ("S ↦ t_P(S) is continuous ... (z,S) ↦ χ(|z|)t_P(S) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G)"), used in its steps 4(iii) and 7. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n (compact, Grassmannian.instCompactSpace); H^n := μHE[n]; unitBallVolume n is the extended-real volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal; μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^n⌞T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)); p_S := Grassmannian.project S = Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S; t_P(S) := ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap S − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖ (operator norm of p_S − p_P).
1. Let b be the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^N (EuclideanSpace.basisFun) and Φ : Matrix(Fin N, Fin N, ℝ) → (ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N) the composite of the linear equivalences (LinearMap.toMatrix b b).symm and LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap. Φ is linear on a finite-dimensional space, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional).
2. By definition projectionLinearMap S = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b).symm S.1 (b is Grassmannian.coordinateBasis), so by linearity projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b).symm (S.1 − P.1) and toContinuousLinearMap(projectionLinearMap S − projectionLinearMap P) = Φ(S.1 − P.1).
3. Hence t_P(S) = ‖Φ(S.1 − P.1)‖ is continuous in S (S ↦ S.1 is continuous, then subtraction of a constant, Φ, and the norm).
4. F(z,S) := χ(z)·t_P(S) is continuous (product of χ ∘ Prod.fst and t_P ∘ Prod.snd).
5. support F ⊆ (support χ) × G ⊆ tsupport χ × G, a closed set, so tsupport F ⊆ tsupport χ × G (closure_minimal).
6. tsupport χ × G is compact (χ has compact support, G is compact), so F has compact support. Thus F defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ), f(z,S) = χ(z)t_P(S) by definition, and tsupport f ⊆ tsupport χ × G by 5.

1. Apply (hA) to N, n, Λ (1 ≤ n, 1 ≤ Λ) and take the resulting δ̄, c₀. Fix δ, ε, m, k₀, U, W, P, g, φ as in the statement. ω ∈ (0,∞) and unitBallVolume n = ofReal ω. Put L := 4ε/ω; then 0 < L ≤ 1 (4ε ≤ ω). Write μ := μ_W and p := p_P, a continuous linear map; P.plane is closed, hence Borel.
2. Bad set. (hA)(a),(b) apply to (δ, ε, U, W, P) because B°_3(0) ⊆ U, W has locally bounded first variation, and the three smallness hypotheses hold. Call y good if (1) and (2) hold at y. With E := {y ∈ B_2(0) ∩ spt μ : y not good}, (a) gives μ(E) ≤ c₀ε. Let E' := toMeasurable μ E: Borel, E ⊆ E', μ(E') = μ(E).
3. Canonical form. The sibling canonical_domination (with (hD), (hC); W is integral with locally bounded first variation) gives θ, IsVarifoldOf W M θ with M := {x ∈ spt μ : W has a tangent plane at x}, for every x ∈ M a tangent plane with multiplicity θ(x) and HasDensity n μ x (ofReal θ(x)), H^n(Z) = 0 for Z := {x ∈ M : θ(x) is not a positive integer}, and the domination inequality.
4. Good flat points. G' := (M ∖ Z) ∩ E'ᶜ ∩ {|p y| < 1} ∩ {|y − p y| < ε}. G' is H^n-null-measurable: M is H^n-null-measurable (IsVarifoldOf), Z is H^n-null, E' is Borel, the last two sets are open.
5. Let y ∈ G'. Then |y| ≤ |p y| + |y − p y| < 1 + ε ≤ 2, so y ∈ B_2(0); y ∈ spt μ since M ⊆ spt μ; y is good (otherwise y ∈ E ⊆ E'); and θ(y) = m_y for an integer m_y ≥ 1 (y ∉ Z).
6. Graph cover. (TGC) with N, n, L ∈ (0,1], U, W, P gives closed Γ_i with |(y−z) − p(y−z)| ≤ L|p(y−z)| on each Γ_i, containing every point at which W has a tangent plane T with |p_T v − p v| ≤ (L/4)|v| ∀v. 7. Fibre sums. Let a ∈ P.plane, |a| < 1, and s a finite set of points y ∈ G' with p y = a. Apply (hA)(b) with x := a and Θ := ofReal ∘ θ: for y ∈ s we have p y = a, y ∈ B_2(0) ∩ spt μ, (1), (2), |y − p y| < ε (step 5), HasDensity n μ y (ofReal θ(y)) (step 3) and ofReal θ(y) = m_y ≥ 1. Hence Σ_{y∈s} ofReal θ(y) ≤ ofReal(1+δ)μ(B_1(a))/unitBallVolume n + ofReal δ ≤ ofReal(1+δ)·ofReal(mω)/ofReal(ω) + ofReal δ = ofReal((1+δ)m + δ) < k₀ + 1, using the hypothesis μ(B_1(a)) ≤ ofReal(mω), unitBallVolume n = ofReal ω, m ≥ 0, ω > 0 and (1+δ)m + δ < k₀ + 1.

Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the parent theorem intcpt_flat_limit_integer_multiplicity (case n = 0: the weights are sums of integer point masses, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → θ₀, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ); the last step uses closedness of ℕ in ℝ instead of eventual constancy. Notation: G := Grassmannian N 0; H^0 := μHE[0]; μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^0⌞T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)). (H) denotes the hypothesis ∫ f dW_k → θ₀ ∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G.
1. dim P.plane = 0 (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so P.plane = ⊥ (Submodule.finrank_eq_zero) and P.plane = {0} as a set.
2. H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 for every x (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Consequently ∫_{P.plane} g dH^0 = ∫_{{0}} g dH^0 = H^0{0}·g(0) = g(0) for every g (integral_singleton).
3. Claim: for every k, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)).toReal is a natural number (μ_k := μ_{W_k}).
  3a. IsIntegral W_k gives M, θ with IsVarifoldOf W_k M θ and θ ∈ ℕ for (H^0⌞M)-a.e. point.
  3b. M is countable: CountablyRectifiable 0 M gives M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^0(M₀) = 0 and F_j : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) → ℝ^N. M₀ = ∅ because any x ∈ M₀ would give 1 = H^0{x} ≤ H^0(M₀) = 0. The domain of F_j is a subsingleton, so range F_j = {F_j(0)}. Hence M ⊆ ⋃_j {F_j(0)} is countable.
  3c. θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M: with Bad := {x : θ(x) ∉ ℕ}, H^0(Bad ∩ M) ≤ (H^0⌞M)(Bad) = 0 (Measure.le_restrict_apply and the a.e. statement), and a point of Bad ∩ M would have H^0-measure 1 ≤ 0.
  3d. B := B_{1/2}(0) is Borel. μ_k(B) = W_k.measure(B × G) (Varifold.weight_apply) = ∫⁻_S ofReal θ dH^0 by IsVarifoldOf, where S := {x ∈ M : ∃ S', (weighted approximate tangent at x) ∧ (x,S') ∈ B × G} ⊆ M is countable. By lintegral_countable, this equals Σ'_{x∈S} ofReal θ(x)·H^0{x} = Σ'_{x∈S} (⌊θ(x)⌋₊ : [0,∞]) (θ(x) is a natural number by 3c, so ofReal θ(x) = ⌊θ(x)⌋₊).
  3e. If this sum is ∞, its toReal is 0 ∈ ℕ. Otherwise only finitely many x ∈ S have ⌊θ(x)⌋₊ ≥ 1 (ENNReal.finite_const_le_of_tsum_ne_top with ε = 1) and all other terms are 0, so the sum equals the finite sum Σ ⌊θ(x)⌋₊ over that finite set (tsum_eq_sum), the cast of a natural number; its toReal is that natural number.
4. Cutoffs. g₁(x) := max(0, min(1, 2 − 4|x|)) and g₂(x) := max(0, min(1, 3 − 4|x|)) are continuous and [0,1]-valued; g₁ = 0 for |x| ≥ 1/2, g₂ = 1 for |x| ≤ 1/2, both vanish for |x| ≥ 3/4 (so tsupport g_i ⊆ B_{3/4}(0), which is compact and contained in B°_5(0)), and g₁(0) = g₂(0) = 1.
5. By the sibling weight_tendsto and 2, ∫ g_i dμ_k → θ₀∫_{P.plane} g_i dH^0 = θ₀g_i(0) = θ₀ (i = 1, 2).
6. μ_k(B_{3/4}(0)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact), and |g_i| ≤ 1 vanishes off B_{3/4}(0), so g_i is μ_k-integrable. Since g₁ ≤ 1_{B_{1/2}(0)} ≤ g₂ pointwise: ofReal(∫ g₁ dμ_k) = ∫⁻ ofReal g₁ dμ_k ≤ μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal g₂ dμ_k = ofReal(∫ g₂ dμ_k) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, lintegral_indicator_one, lintegral_mono).
7. By 5, 6, continuity of ofReal and the squeeze theorem, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → ofReal θ₀ in [0,∞]. As ofReal θ₀ ≠ ∞, toReal is continuous there (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)).toReal → (ofReal θ₀).toReal = θ₀ (θ₀ ≥ 0).
8. The range of ℕ → ℝ is closed (Nat.isClosedEmbedding_coe_real). By 3 every term of the real sequence in 7 lies in it, so its limit θ₀ lies in it (IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto): θ₀ = m for some m ∈ ℕ.

toReal of the masses are naturals converging to θ₀; ℕ is closed in ℝ, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ.
